design_principles: Each pollster starts from its own last published value, so persistent house effects are not estimated twice.
Retention is a scenario assumption about fieldwork timing and projection smoothing, not a disclosed pollster coefficient.
Sampling and fieldwork error is used in simulation draws, never added to the deterministic central estimate.
A Sonntagsfrage is a current-attitude measurement; only FGW explicitly distinguishes raw political mood from a projection model.

publicly_disclosed.sampling_mode: representative online survey supported by a permanent telephone survey (Perpetua Demoscopia)
publicly_disclosed.additional_model: Potentiale: secure vote, maximum potential, negative Sonntagsfrage; constituency map statically downscales the latest national result

publicly_disclosed.sampling_mode: random telephone selection; household respondent selected by last-birthday method; dual-frame studies can include mobile numbers
publicly_disclosed.panel_note: forsa.omninet households are recruited representatively and cannot self-enrol

publicly_disclosed.sampling_mode: random fixed-line, random mobile, and one-time SMS-link online subsamples
publicly_disclosed.sample_design: east Germany oversampled, then corrected; dual-frame design weights
publicly_disclosed.weighting: selection probability correction plus nonresponse adjustment to sex, age and education benchmarks
publicly_disclosed.political_mood: weighted answers to the vote-intention question
publicly_disclosed.projection: adds longer-term political convictions, party attachments and tactical considerations collected through additional indicators
publicly_disclosed.reported_margin_pp: about 2 pp at 10%, about 3 pp at 40% for n≈1250
